Simulated geospatial data

Source: R/sim.R
rcs_sim_polygons.Rd

Polygons, points, lines and a raster in a box of open ocean: longitude -30 to -24, latitude 6 to 9, EPSG:4326. The box is cut by an edge between two H3 cells of resolution 0, so the shapes exercise every level of the H3 grid. The result is the same for the same arguments; the random number stream of the session is not changed.

Usage

rcs_sim_polygons(n = 1000, seed = 1, crossing_share = 0.1, special = FALSE)

rcs_sim_points(n = 1000, seed = 1)

rcs_sim_lines(n = 1000, seed = 1)

rcs_sim_raster(seed = 1, nrow = 1000, ncol = 1000)

Arguments

n

Number of rows (without the two special rows); at least 20 for polygons, at least 0 for points and lines.

seed

Seed of the generator.

crossing_share

Share of rows built to cross H3 cell edges of resolution 5, between 0 and 0.5.

special

Add the antimeridian and the pole polygon.

nrow, ncol

Size of the raster in cells.

Value

rcs_sim_polygons(): an sf tibble with the columns id (integer), area (double, square kilometres, NA for the empty geometry), cat (character, a to e) and geometry (polygons and multipolygons). It needs the h3o package.

rcs_sim_points(): an sf tibble with the columns id (integer), value (double), cat (character) and geometry (points spread evenly over the box).

rcs_sim_lines(): an sf tibble with the columns id (integer), length (double, kilometres), cat (character) and geometry (lines of two to six vertices, up to some tens of kilometres long).

rcs_sim_raster(): a terra::SpatRaster over the box with the layers height (double, smooth), cover (integer classes 1 to 5) and moisture (double, with missing cells). It needs the terra package.

Details

rcs_sim_polygons() returns rows of three groups, in this order of id:

  • id 1 to 9, fixed shapes: (1) a rectangle with four vertices that covers more than 100 H3 cells of resolution 5; (2) a large polygon with many vertices; (3) a large polygon with a hole; (4) a thin polygon about 300 km long and 100 m wide; (5 to 7) multipolygons, the last with parts in different cells; (8) a polygon across the edge between the two resolution-0 cells; (9) an empty geometry.

  • then round(crossing_share * n) small squares centred on a vertex of an H3 cell of resolution 5, so each crosses cell edges;

  • then small squares and hexagons of 0.01 to 0.5 square kilometres at random places.

With special = TRUE, two rows outside the box follow, both in open ocean: id n + 1, a polygon across the antimeridian (longitude 179 to -179, latitude 6 to 9), and id n + 2, a polygon around the north pole (above latitude 88).

For a projected case, transform the result: sf::st_transform(rcs_sim_polygons(), 32626).

Examples

rcs_sim_polygons(30)
#> Simple feature collection with 30 features and 3 fields (with 1 geometry empty)
#> Geometry type: GEOMETRY
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -29.8 ymin: 6.1 xmax: -24.55762 ymax: 8.700378
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#> # A tibble: 30 × 4
#>       id       area cat                                                 geometry
#>    <int>      <dbl> <chr>                                         <GEOMETRY [°]>

#>  6     6     0.392  e     MULTIPOLYGON (((-27.96559 7.733237, -27.96159 7.73323…
#>  7     7     0.391  a     MULTIPOLYGON (((-26.42263 8.281812, -26.41863 8.28181…
#>  8     8     4.90   a     POLYGON ((-27.59022 7.49, -27.57022 7.49, -27.57022 7…
